mechanism_narrative: The recent sustained upward trend in RETAIL_REC mobility, moving from -41.9% to -34.1% over the last three weeks, indicates a recovery that will continue, leading to higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: The mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the mean RETAIL_REC over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES mobility, currently at -28.3%, continues its recent upward trend and crosses the -25% from baseline threshold, it signals a significant return to offices, driving increased weekday retail and recreation activity over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: WORKPLACES rises above -25% from baseline, but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the mean of the previous 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: The concurrent and sustained upward trend in both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES mobility indicates a broader return to daily routines and commuting, which synergistically boosts retail and recreation footfall over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both increase week-on-week for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: Both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES mobility increase for two consecutive weeks, but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not increase relative to the previous 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: In a reopening regime, a sustained decrease in RESIDENTIAL mobility, as observed from 19.4% to 16.9% over the last two weeks, indicates people are spending less time at home, directly translating to more out-of-home activities including retail and recreation over the next week.
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL mobility falls for two consecutive weeks, but RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days does not increase.

mechanism_narrative: Increased PARKS mobility, currently at -31.3% and trending upwards, suggests a general comfort with public spaces and outdoor activities, which often precedes or accompanies a willingness to engage in other out-of-home activities like retail and recreation over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS mobility rises above -30% from baseline
failure_condition: PARKS mobility rises above -30% from baseline, but RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days does not show an increase.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL mobility remains high (above 15%) while GROCERY_PHARM mobility also increases (above 5%), it suggests a preference for essential errands and staying home, diverting activity away from discretionary retail and recreation over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL > 15% and GROCERY_PHARM > 5% for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL mobility remains high (>15%) and GROCERY_PHARM mobility increases (>5%) for two consecutive weeks, but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days increases.

mechanism_narrative: A significant week-on-week increase in TRANSIT mobility, currently at -33.9% and showing a recent upward trend, indicates a policy-driven or confidence-driven return to public transport, which directly facilitates access to retail and recreation venues over the next week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT increases by more than 2 points week-on-week
failure_condition: TRANSIT mobility increases by more than 2 points week-on-week, but RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days decreases.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained high level of GROCERY_PHARM mobility, especially if it's trending upwards (currently 8.7%) while other discretionary categories lag, suggests a focus on essential needs, potentially diverting disposable income and time away from discretionary retail and recreation over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM remains above 5% for 3 consecutive weeks
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM remains above 5% for 3 consecutive weeks, but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days increases compared to the previous 28 days.
